newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Colgate-Palmolive scores partial Brazil win.
newsitem.headline: Colgate-Palmolive scores partial Brazil win.

text.p: The $1.04 billion purchase by Colgate-Palmolive of Brazilan oral hygiene firm Anakol has been approved by a government anti-trust body but the U.S. giant must opt for one of three tough conditions linked to the approval.
The Administrative Economic Defence Council (Cade) voted late on Wednesday in favor of the buyout but said Colgate-Palmolive must either:
-- refrain for four years from selling the Kolynos brand of toothpaste produced by Anakol;
-- licence Kolynos to a third party over a 20-year period;
-- sell the Kolynos brand to a competitor with a less than
one percent share of the market.
Colgate-Palmolive has 60 days to choose one of the options.
Kolynos accounts for about 50 percent of Brazilian toothpaste sales and gave Colgate-Palmolive a roughly 77 percent total share of the market.
Anakol manufactures Kolynos in several Latin American countries. The Brazilian operations accounted for $760 million of the 1995 buyout.
Cade investigated the deal to see if it stifled competition in Brazil or prevented new players from entering the market.
Cade did not impose any restrictions on Kolynos' other oral hygiene products, like toothbrushes and mouthwashes.
"We won because Cade approved the operation despite the conditions," Carlos Eduardo Toro, Colgate-Palmolive's vice-president in Brazil, was quoted as saying by newspaper Gazata Mercantil.
Rivals also claimed victory. "We see Cade's decision as positive for the consumer and for competition," a director of Procter & Gamble's Brazilian subsidiary told Gazeta.
